title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: A label hidden by mistake comes back
summary: Corrects yesterday's change, which could hide a hint that was still worth showing.

highlights.title: Arguments That Carry On To The Next Line
highlights.description: Yesterday's change read only to the end of the line, so a name alone on its line looked like the whole argument even when the expression continued below, and its label was dropped. A label is now dropped only when the argument really ends there.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Yesterday the extension stopped labelling an argument whose name already matches the parameter. The text it reads for an argument stops at the end of the line, so a name sitting alone on its line looked like the whole argument even when the expression carried on below, as in a name on one line followed by a chained call on the next. The label was then dropped although the value passed was no longer that variable. A label is now dropped only when the argument really ends there, which the closing bracket or the comma on the next line tells us.

A missing label is invisible, unlike a wrong one, which is why this is worth a release of its own even though the reference project, 3187 Kotlin files, does not format arguments that way and loses none.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: The counts on that project are unchanged by this release: 11483 parameter labels, 1246 type labels, no redundant label left.
No new commands or settings in this release.
